classification.difficultyReason: Match vertices in overlapping triangles using marked and common angles, then identify corresponding sides.

content.prompt: Copy and complete each similarity statement, giving the similarity test and naming the vertices in matching order. Then copy and complete the ratio statement.

spec.description: A, X and C are collinear in that order. Triangles ABC and AMX lie on opposite sides of AC. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Angles BAX and XAM are labelled alpha; angles ABC and AMX are labelled theta. All five vertices and five required segments are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; no matching-order or ratio answers.

answer.worked:
$\angle BAC=\angle MAX=\alpha$ and $\angle ABC=\angle AMX=\theta$ (given).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle AMX$ (AAA), with $A\leftrightarrow A$, $B\leftrightarrow M$, $C\leftrightarrow X$.

Matching sides give $\dfrac{AB}{AM}=\dfrac{BC}{MX}$.

spec.description: Triangles ABC and APB share AB; P is directly below B. Both right-angle markers and both alpha labels are retained. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: CAB and BAP are labelled alpha; ABC and APB are marked right angles.

answer.worked:
$\angle CAB=\angle BAP=\alpha$ and $\angle ABC=\angle APB=90^\circ$ (given).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle APB$ (AAA), with $A\leftrightarrow A$, $B\leftrightarrow P$, $C\leftrightarrow B$.

Matching sides give $\dfrac{AB}{AP}=\dfrac{BC}{PB}$.

spec.description: P lies on AC and Q on BC; AB and PQ are horizontal. No parallel arrows are added. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: BAC and QPC are labelled theta. The smaller triangle shares angle C with ABC.

answer.worked:
$\angle BAC=\angle QPC=\theta$ (given), and $\angle ACB=\angle PCQ$ (common angle).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle PQC$ (AAA), with $A\leftrightarrow P$, $B\leftrightarrow Q$, $C\leftrightarrow C$.

Matching sides give $\dfrac{AB}{PQ}=\dfrac{BC}{QC}$.

spec.description: C lies on AD in triangle ABD, and BC is drawn. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: ABC and BDA are labelled alpha; the triangles share angle A.

answer.worked:
$\angle ABC=\angle ADB=\alpha$ (given), and $\angle BAC=\angle DAB$ (common angle).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle ADB$ (AAA), with $A\leftrightarrow A$, $B\leftrightarrow D$, $C\leftrightarrow B$.

Matching sides give $\dfrac{AB}{AD}=\dfrac{BC}{DB}$.
